text: EMG activity of the pectoralis major during traditional lifting was markedly higher on the concentric portion of the movement (by 18%, 19%, and 12% for the first, middle, and last repetition, respectively). During eccentric actions, the activation advantage for training at a traditional versus a slow tempo increased to 32%, 36%, and 36% in the first, middle, and last repetition, respectively. These findings provide evidence that volitionally slowing the tempo during a repetition is suboptimal for maximally activating the target muscle.
book: Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy
chapter: Chapter 4: Role of Resistance Training Variables in Hypertrophy
